hero.title: Frankencoin|governance
hero.subtitle: Anyone can propose a new collateral or minting module. Holders of Frankencoin Shares (FCS) review it and can veto. Nothing needs a majority vote to pass.

steps.title: Submit
steps.body: Anyone opens a proposal on-chain and pays a fee that goes to the reserve. A new collateral is proposed by opening the first position; a new minting module by a minter application.

steps.title: Review
steps.body: The proposal is public for a set period: at least five days for a collateral, longer for minting modules. The community discusses it and publishes assessments.

steps.title: Veto or go live
steps.body: Any FCS holder, or group, with more than 1% of voting power can veto. If no one does, the proposal is live. Exactly 1% is not enough.

items.title: Collateral and minters
items.description: Which assets can back ZCHF and which modules may mint it; both can be vetoed.

items.title: Interest rates
items.description: The borrowing and savings rates, proposed by qualified FCS holders with a seven-day grace period.

items.title: Cross-chain settings
items.description: Which chains ZCHF bridges to and the rate limits of the bridge.

power.title: Voting power comes from holding, not just balance
power.body: Votes grow with the number of shares and how long they have been held; a transferred balance starts its holding time at zero. Votes can be delegated, and a holder may spend votes to cancel another holder's votes. The full rules, including how legacy FPS votes are credited, are in the documentation.

fcs.title: About Frankencoin Shares
fcs.body: How FCS relates to the reserve, how to acquire shares and the risks of holding them are covered on the FCS page.

end.title: Take part
end.body: Review open proposals, publish an assessment, or hold FCS and build voting power.
